title: The Four Dimensions and External Factors

header.html: The ITIL Four Dimensions of Product and Service Management (10%)
List the four dimensions; understand the importance of each; explain the holistic approach; know the external factors (PESTLE)
the official ITIL Foundation (Version 5) syllabus, version 5.0 (February 2026), category 2

toc.title: Each dimension in a little more detail

html:
1Why four dimensions

Every product and service must be looked at through four dimensions at the same time. If one is ignored, value suffers. This is the holistic approach: think about all four together, not one at a time.

Dimension What it covers
Organizations and people Structure, roles, culture, skills, leadership, communication
Information and technology Data, knowledge, tools, platforms, automation, AI
Partners and suppliers Relationships with other organizations that supply or support the work
Value streams and processes The activities and flows that turn demand into value

Old wording ITIL 4 called these the "four dimensions of service management". Version 5 says product and service management.

2Each dimension in a little more detail

Dimension Typical questions Example
Organizations and people Who does what? Do they have the skills? Is the culture right? Cross-functional product teams, clear roles, training
Information and technology What information and tools are needed? Is data protected and usable? A monitoring platform, a knowledge base, AI assistants
Partners and suppliers Which outside parties are involved? How are contracts and relationships managed? A cloud provider, a development partner
Value streams and processes What steps create value? Where are the waits and waste? A request-to-fulfillment flow with automation
Exam tip

. People and culture = organizations and people. Tools and data = information and technology. Outside parties = partners and suppliers. Steps and flow = value streams and processes.

3External factors: PESTLE

The dimensions are influenced from outside. PESTLE lists the external factors:

Letter Factor Example
P Political Government policy, trade rules
E Economic Inflation, exchange rates, funding
S Social Customer expectations, working habits
T Technological New tools, AI, standards
L Legal Privacy and data laws, contracts
E Environmental Climate rules, energy use
Exam tip

. PESTLE = Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, Environmental. The list is for external factors; internal factors are the four dimensions themselves.

Exam tip

. If an option names a dimension that is not one of the four (for example "governance" or "practices"), it is a distractor. Only organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, value streams and processes count.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team has the right tools but nobody trained to use them. Which dimension is weakest?

  • AInformation and technology
  • BOrganizations and people
  • CPartners and suppliers
  • DValue streams and processes
Show the answer

Answer: B. Skills and roles belong to organizations and people.

S2Which statement about the four dimensions is CORRECT? (1) They should be considered together. (2) One dimension can be ignored if the others are strong. (3) Partners and suppliers is one of the four. (4) PESTLE is a list of the four dimensions.

  • A1 and 3
  • B2 and 4
  • C1 and 4
  • D2 and 3
Show the answer

Answer: A. The four dimensions are used together, and partners and suppliers is one of them.

S3New privacy legislation forces a change in how customer data is stored. Which PESTLE factor is this?

  • APolitical
  • BSocial
  • CLegal
  • DEconomic
Show the answer

Answer: C. Laws and regulations are the legal factor.

S4Identify the missing word(s). The [ ? ] dimension covers the activities and flows that turn demand into value.

  • AValue streams and processes
  • BInformation and technology
  • CPartners and suppliers
  • DOrganizations and people
Show the answer

Answer: A. That describes value streams and processes.

S5A company relies on an outside vendor to run its help desk. Which dimension does managing that vendor fall under?

  • AInformation and technology
  • BPartners and suppliers
  • COrganizations and people
  • DValue streams and processes
Show the answer

Answer: B. Relationships with outside parties are partners and suppliers.

S6Why does ITIL stress a holistic approach to the four dimensions?

  • ASo that all four are balanced and no weak dimension undermines value
  • BSo that only technology gets funding
  • CSo that each dimension is optimized alone, whatever the others do
  • DSo that PESTLE factors can be ignored
Show the answer

Answer: A. Value suffers when any dimension is neglected.

4.2 Recall questions

R1List the four dimensions.

Show the answer

Organizations and people; information and technology; partners and suppliers; value streams and processes.

R2What does PESTLE stand for?

Show the answer

Political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental.

R3Which dimension covers data, tools and AI?

Show the answer

Information and technology.

R4Which dimension covers culture and skills?

Show the answer

Organizations and people.

R5What is the holistic approach?

Show the answer

Considering all four dimensions together.

R6Are PESTLE factors internal or external?

Show the answer

External.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Four dimensions organizations and people; information and technology; partners and suppliers; value streams and processes
Holistic all four together
PESTLE political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental (external)
Old wording "four dimensions of service management"
